outcome.technical:
THE RULE (written before code). An entry names a left-out path when its command's text holds that path's last component as a whole name - no letter or digit runs on into it through the characters that join a name (._-+@~) on either side - and, for a path known to be a directory, with a / or \ separator directly beside it. The text is searched as written and once more as a shell's quote removal leaves it, never split into words, so no quote, escape, delimiter or whitespace kind can hide an occurrence and nothing in the reading can fail or recurse. FAILURE DIRECTIONS: a command that is not text grades (measured, UNREADABLE reason); over-reads (a path in a comment/echo, a sibling directory sharing a left-out directory's last component, two unquoted words spelling a spaced path, a literal path a shell would glue a word onto) grade (a run measured); kept under-reads, each a stale green, stated beside UNREADABLE and pinned by lw22: a bare $VAR, a glob, an ancestor directory (docs/audit, .), a left-out directory named by its bare last component after a cd, a brace expansion. Fixed by the invariant: a path through .. and a name assembled from quoted pieces are now read (lw22). CHANGES in plugins/audit/scripts/governance/run-test-gate.py: _command_words, _word_rels, _names_path, _WORD_PIECES and the posixpath import removed; added _quote_removed, _reaches_letter, _holds_name, _last_name, _NAME_JOINERS, _SEPARATORS; UNSPLITTABLE renamed UNREADABLE ('its command is not text'); grades_left_out(gate, excluded, directories=()) drops the roots parameter (an absolute path holds the relative path's last component, so no root is needed; no caller outside this file passed it). (3) reuse_identity now grades _grading_steps(commands, build): every step under its declared command AND the command that runs; declared_gate resolves a step named affected/phase-gate: <entry> to its entry's build command (_declared_entry, _PHASE_GATE_STEP, which the arm-step builder now also spells). Consequence: a stored row whose gate held a phase-gate arm step keys differently once (one measurement after upgrade, never a stale repeat). ACCEPTANCE 3/4: an entry the old code called unsplittable (unbalanced quote, apostrophe in double quotes) is read for literal names like any other - it grades only if it names a left-out path, with the 'names' sentence. The 'cannot be read for the paths it names' sentence is still printed, byte for byte, but only for a command that is not text (lw9, lw21 pin its prefix); whether the manifest validator lets a non-string build command through was not checked. Both prefixes in drive-phase.py GATE_LEFT_OUT still match; drive-phase.py untouched. outcome.descriptive: Whether a gate step may be repeated is now decided by a whole-name search of the command's text, so delimiters, whitespace kinds, apostrophes, Windows separators and phase-gate arm steps can no longer hide a left-out path, and nothing in the reading can raise.
